newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BHP sees one integrated steel mill.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BHP sees one integrated steel mill.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd said on Tuesday that it saw the logic of having only one integrated steel operation in Australia.

"Our current plans are to initially increase Port Kembla to five million tonnes a year, but ultimately we will see the logic of integrated steel making driving us towards one integrated steel operation in Australia," BHP Steel chief executive Ron McNeilly told reporters.
He said this was likely to happen around the years 2005 to 2010.
BHP announced earlier it would phase out steelmaking at its Newcastle plant by the end of 1999 and that it planned to close its Geelong rod mill and Sydney wire mill in 1999.
McNeilly also said he foresaw that BHP's three hot strip mills, in Port Kembla (New South Wales), Western Port (Victoria) and New Zealand, would also be rolled into one world scale facility.

"There's a very strong case over time for those three mills to be combined into one major world class, world scale facility. over time, more like 10 years, the world, with big integrated steel operations and big flat products facilities, is moving towards scale and centralisation and towards world economies of scale," McNeilly said.
